instrument_or_setup.value: Conventional constant acceleration Doppler velocity drive with 57Co (Rh-matrix) source; transmission geometry; velocity of the drive calibrated by a pure iron (α-Fe) foil; spectra fitted with the NORMOS program (B_hf probability distribution up to 40 sextets).

purpose.value: Examine the local atomic configurations of Fe in the Fe-5Al powder sample and detect ordered-phase (DO3) formation / solid solution of Al.

key_findings.value: The Fe-5Al Mössbauer spectrum was deconvoluted (NORMOS) into two components: B_hf = 32.67 T with area 24% and V_f 23.55% (assigned (8Fe)nn + (5Fe+1Al)nnn), and B_hf = 30.65 T with area 51.6% and V_f 50.7% (assigned (7Fe+1Al)nn + (6Fe)nnn or (8Fe)nn + (6Al)nnn). The P(B_hf) hump is broad and deconvoluted into multiple peaks spanning roughly 26–34 T. The hyperfine field decreases as the number of Al nearest neighbours increases (non-magnetic Al). The ~23 T peak observed for Fe-6Al, Fe-6.8Al and Fe-9Al (possible Fe3Al indicator) is ABSENT for Fe-5Al, attributed to a low volume fraction of the Fe3Al phase.

instrument_or_setup.value: Laboratory-based dual energy Mo-Cr-SAXS system (Xeuss, Xenocs, France); dual X-ray energies and camera lengths of 550 and 2400 mm; powder sandwiched between Scotch Magic tape (3M, USA); 2D profiles azimuthally integrated to 1D using FIT2D software; intensities converted to absolute scale with glassy carbon secondary standard; scattering angle calibrated with Silver-Behenate powder.

measurement_conditions.value: Transmission geometry; measurement time 4–6 h; q-range from 0.0254 to 10 nm⁻¹

purpose.value: Quantitatively estimate the size, volume fraction and number density of the ordered DO3 (Fe3Al) phase in the Fe-5Al powder sample.

key_findings.value: A weak nano-sized ordered-phase scattering peak is observed between q = 0.3–3 nm⁻¹. For the 5 wt% Al (Fe-5Al) composition, the Fe3Al ordered-phase diameter is ~2.5 ± 0.15 nm and the volume fraction is just below 0.5%. At low q (below 0.3 nm⁻¹) the intensity decays as q⁻⁴ (Porod scattering), assigned to larger heterogeneities (grains/grain boundaries); at high q (> 3 nm⁻¹) an incoherent flat background appears. SAXS volume fractions are lower than the Mössbauer-traced DO3 fractions.

unmapped_findings: For the Fe-5Al powder sample the ~23 T Mössbauer hyperfine-field peak (observed for Fe-6Al, Fe-6.8Al and Fe-9Al and taken as a possible indicator of Fe3Al phase with low volume fraction) is absent, which the authors attribute to the low volume fraction of Fe3Al phase in Fe-5Al (b0047).

The Fe-5Al sample, like the other Fe-Al compositions, shows a broadened six-line Mössbauer sextet relative to the α-Fe foil, evidencing that Al addition alters the local Fe atomic configurations and creates new lower hyperfine-field components (figure_001, b0047).

SAXS scattering intensity of the Fe-Al low-density steels increases with Al content (5→9 wt%) implying an increase of the nano-sized ordered phase, and the Guinier regions shift towards low q confirming increasing ordered-phase size; at low q (below 0.3 nm⁻¹) intensity decays as q⁻⁴ indicating larger heterogeneities such as grains/grain boundaries (b0050).

The SAXS volume fractions of the ordered phase are lower than the DO3 volume fractions traced by Mössbauer spectroscopy because SAXS gives collective information about ordered phase having a sharper boundary whereas Mössbauer traces all local environments including those with diffused boundaries (b0050).
